summary: Texas Forest Service lookout in Panola County that shares its name with the Snap community; Coast and Geodetic Survey first observed its station in 1958; listed as gone; no site description found.

facts.status_note: Listed as gone on the Forest Fire Lookout Association's Texas list; no source describes what remains at the site

events.note: Coast and Geodetic Survey first observed the station and described it; the datasheet marks the station as a lookout tower

evidence.supports: Snap is a farming community in southwestern Panola County, about six miles southwest of Carthage
evidence.quote: Snap, a farming community off State Highway 315 six miles southwest of Carthage in southwestern Panola County

evidence.supports: in the mid-1930s the community had a store, a church, a cemetery and houses, with seven residents in 1936
evidence.quote: In the mid-1930s Snap consisted of a store, a church, a cemetery, and a number of houses; the community reported seven residents in 1936.

evidence.supports: by the early 1990s the community had only a cemetery and a few dwellings
evidence.quote: By the early 1990s only a cemetery and a few scattered dwellings remained.

evidence.supports: the Coast and Geodetic Survey first observed the station in 1958
the datasheet marks the station as a lookout tower
the Texas list records the tower as gone

sources.title: Snap, TX
sources.publisher: Texas State Historical Association, Handbook of Texas

sources.title: NGS Data Sheet for station CR1127 (SNAP LOOKOUT TOWER)

notes_for_editor: Thin record. The NGS datasheet's 1958 note says 'SEE STATION SNAP', which points to a separate station description we did not find. Its orthometric height of 112 m (367 ft) was scaled from a topographic map and is ground elevation at the survey mark, not tower height, so it is not used. No build date, height, design or staffing found. Access and current condition unknown.
